excerpts.author: jimmygchen
excerpts.content:
I had local interop working with geth. The geth impl is interopable but haven't offload the computation, so it might actually be more CPU intensive than the existing CL-only PeerDAS implementation

The images used are here:
https://notes.ethereum.org/@ethpandaops/peerdas-devnet-6#

excerpts.author: parithosh
excerpts.content: ooo this is amazing finding! wdym by hasn't offloaded computation? are we just computing things on the EL and CL right now?

excerpts.author: jimmygchen
excerpts.content: Computation happens in geth right now whenever we call getPayload and get blobs as a quick way to have something interop-able, so we still need the complete implementation to have the gains

excerpts.author: jimmygchen
excerpts.content: Note that because it happens on demand, it takes longer for geth to respond, so shorter slot time may not work

excerpts.author: manunlp
excerpts.content:
So the issue was, for some reason, some Prysm nodes were stopped and restarted during the first epoch after genesis.
There is a known issue where Prysm cannot sync when it was stopped during the first epoch after genesis.
==> The workaround is to wipe the DB and resync, which worked.

excerpts.content: (First epoch was deneb for information)
